posts.name: Kaivax
posts.cooked:
The WoW Forever Beta is now closed, and we’re incredibly grateful to everyone who joined us over the last five weeks of playtesting, data gathering, bug reporting, and feedback.

We’re now quickly moving into a period of a few short days where we will do some focused work on priority issues and the game service itself, so that it will be in good shape for launch day on November 4.

And of course, we’ll open access to the character creation system on Tuesday, October 27, allowing everyone plenty of time to select the ruleset that will define your journey and snag the name that best fits your adventurer.

image800×381 122 KB

You won’t have to wait until the game launches to make these big decisions.

Also next week, we’re going to continue with our WoW Forever Podcast. If you haven’t consumed it all, this is a great time to catch up with everything the WoW Forever designers have had to say.

  • The WoW: Forever Podcast: Episode 1 - Unpacking Beta Launch ft. ‪@Xaryu‬
  • The WoW: Forever Podcast: Episode 2 - Speed Running Classes ft. ‪@sodapoppin‬
  • The WoW: Forever Podcast: Episode 3 - Dive Into Dungeons With Devs ft. @Hammerdancegaming
  • The WoW: Forever Podcast: Episode 4 - The PvP Episode ft. ‪@TipsOutBaby‬ & ‪@Savixirl
  • The WoW: Forever Podcast: Episode 5 - End of Beta Special

If you can’t get enough WoW Forever info, we’ve got all kinds of details about the game right here on our website. You can learn more about WoW Forever dungeons here, and the Campfire system here, and raid details here.

Again, we’re deeply grateful to have seen so many people find their Forever home, and create new communities, and find friends (old and new) to join on the journey ahead.

We’re really looking forward to seeing you on November 4! Thank you very much!

image800×400 94.2 KB

you did nothing for shamans. Warcraft is the foundation of world of warcraft and the shaman class should feel like a living continuation of that legacy, When I think thrall, I think a powerful shaman welding the elements calling lightning, summoning an earthquake, commanding the fury of the earth, Embodying the raw elemental power that made the character so iconic though out the franchise.

SO why indeed blizzard are you moving a shaman towards Generic fire spells when there are so many abilities that are rooted in the history of warcraft that could reinforce the identity of this class? Earthquake is a great example. You have decades of lore lean into it!

A shaman is not a spell caster who happens to use elemental magic. The shaman is a spiritual conduit to the elements! a master of the forces of nature and in my opinion one of the most recognizable class fantasies in warcraft. Thrall defined that fantasy, and that legacy should mean something in the way the class is designed and played.

I am not saying developers need to stop innovating. Just innovate in the spirit of warcraft. Give us abilities that feel like they belong to the world that created this class. Because if the class no longer feels inspired by thrall than it no longer belongs in the world.

You are not building on warcraft legacy you’re replacing everything that made it feel special!

posts.cooked:
I had a blast! I got my Human Hunter to level 30, played nearly every day, did some light leveling with alts, and joined an Olympus guild on day one that I quickly grew to enjoy. My experience was full of social interactions, new experiences, and an overall great time!

I loved the new graphics, the campfire system, the updated professions, the pace of the game, the new dungeons, and the absolute wealth of players to interact with.

I was initially against the idea of the Skyborne, but over the course of the beta they grew on me. Far from perfect—and I will continue to bang the drums of war for a true High Elf race for the Alliance—but I will concede that the Skyborne are not terrible. The starter zone was fun, though the story was on the verge of being too grand for a “new adventurer.” Human adventurers are fighting pigs while the Skyborne are mid-crisis trying to save Zepheris Isle and battling an elemental god. I also think the care put into the architecture and zone music pales in comparison to the Blood Elves; I wish the Skyborne had received the same treatment.

That being said, I now think I want to main a Skyborne Hunter for the initial Forever experience instead of a Human. For that, I applaud Blizzard!

Layering was my biggest issue. It broke the immersion and the sense of community I was experiencing. I lost familiar faces as I leveled and traveled the world. I loved how you could quest alongside the same group of players without any direct social interaction—they became fixtures in your world that you had grown to know. Layering destroys that opportunity, and more often than not it was downright jarring.

I am hopeful that Blizzard maintains a strong vision to uphold the promise of “Keeping the WAR in Warcraft” and uses Classic as the foundation for new content. I like the grit, the style, and the friction. I am a firm believer that a game for everyone is a game for no one. Keep politics and social agendas out of Forever—that kind of principle pushes away customers who don’t share those values. The success of the beta and the return of old players should be a clear message that Retail has gone astray and lost many would-be fans due to such poor decisions. Games are meant for gamers, not propaganda. Stick to the pillars that make Classic successful.

Thank you for the beta, and thank you for creating a version of the game that values the core Warcraft players’ feedback! This is the game I want to play for the next 20 years if Blizzard can maintain the pillars they have promised.
